purpose: Close the proven pre-registration cancellation custody gap with an explicit dependency API that moves real resource ownership into SQLx's existing worker/native handle before native open.

authorization.source: Parent /root authorized a minimal dependency-layer static patch after the earlier public-API-only investigation.
authorization.previous_no_fork_scope: The earlier no-fork condition was a research-stage scope constraint, not a permanent user or automatic-approval prohibition.
authorization.performed: Own local files, exact immutable source reads, isolated static git apply, unreachable blobs in the project repository.

exact_source_alignment.scope: All 12 cited Git source files are equal between the commits. SQLite/Core subtrees are equal. All 17 full native receipt files were independently rehashed; all 11 requested Rust files equal their fixed Git counterparts. The native executor, not this agent, extracted and checked the two actual crate archives.

normalized_driver_manifest.dev_dependencies: empty; the new tests use only existing normal dependencies

source_identity.missing_archive_sidecars: Both observed .cargo-checksum.json files were absent; no value was invented.

ownership_chain.meaning: An explicitly supplied Arc owns the actual external resource. Cloned options/pools may hold it longer than any one connection. Replacement of an option does not alter already-created native handles.
from_options clones the opaque owner before the existing SQLx thread::Builder::spawn. No new production task or thread is introduced.

An owned argument remains live across sqlite3_open_v2. A non-NULL returned handle receives it before status errors are examined; the existing error path closes the handle while retaining custody. A NULL result preserves the original OutOfMemory error and has no native SQLite object to protect.

Existing sqlite3_close runs before the owner's field can be dropped. Successful close permits ordinary destruction. Non-OK close first forgets the owner's Option, then keeps the original panic; unwinding cannot release the resource while SQLite may remain live.

behavior_limits: The API does not authenticate a Current receipt, validate authority, lease, expiry, revocation, FinalUse or exact checkpoint cuts.
It does not coordinate transactions or install a commit hook; existing commit-hook semantics remain the independent veto oracle.
The owner must be real and must not retain these options or their pool, which would create an Arc cycle. No Arc-count assertion is used as custody proof.

A failed native close deliberately leaks the retained owner until process exit. Later unsafe external manual close does not recover it. This preserves fail-closed custody at a cost to availability; the original error/panic is not turned into success.

The default None does not change backend selection, SQL, permissions, callback order, close calls or errors. Debug output for the private handle/options acquires an additional optional field, so byte-identical Debug formatting is not claimed.
Existing independent pools/connections that do not opt into this owner are not covered. No current project caller opts in in this candidate.
The earlier registered-collation R2e3 control is not re-labelled full-lifetime coverage. This proposed native token must be adopted and empirically qualified before that open boundary can be closed.

test_controls.name: options::connection_lifetime::tests::cancellation_during_native_open_keeps_resource_custody
test_controls.physical_oracle: A second process opens custody.lock independently. try_lock must be WouldBlock after the connect future and options are dropped while the real sqlite3_open_v2 auto-extension callback remains blocked (gate_status=0). After callback release and observed resource-owner destruction, the same independent probe must succeed.
test_controls.scope: actual native-open cancellation, before a SQLite handle can be returned to the async caller

test_controls.name: options::connection_lifetime::tests::cancellation_during_initial_pragmas_keeps_resource_custody
test_controls.physical_oracle: Drive connect through the establish oneshot with the existing flume async channel and SQLx runtime timeout. A real SQLite progress callback blocks during default initial SQL; cancel the connect future and options, then require the independent process's lock to remain held and gate_status=0. Release the callback and require eventual actual owner release.
test_controls.scope: default initial PRAGMA cancellation, before pool after_connect can install any hook

test_controls.name: options::connection_lifetime::tests::pool_growth_and_cancelled_close_keep_borrowed_connection_custody
test_controls.physical_oracle: Hold five physical pool connections, each with a TEMP marker; close one and prove its replacement has no marker. Poll and cancel the original pool close, close the other four, detach the last live connection, drop the pool and execute a real SELECT. Independent process lock stays held until that connection really closes, then becomes available.
test_controls.scope: growth, physical replacement, borrowed/detached connection and cancelled pool close

test_controls.name: options::connection_lifetime::tests::initialization_error_releases_but_failed_native_close_retains_custody
test_controls.physical_oracle: A real invalid initial PRAGMA retains Database error code 1 and releases the lock after cleanup. A real unfinalized statement then makes sqlite3_close return SQLITE_BUSY; SQLx's original worker panic returns WorkerCrashed, and sqlite3_step still returns SQLITE_ROW. The independent process must still be unable to lock. Even later manual finalization/close cannot reclaim the deliberately forgotten owner; the lock is released only when the owned child exits.
test_controls.scope: ordinary initialization error cleanup and actual failed native close with a live handle

support_entry.name: options::connection_lifetime::tests::owned_scenario
support_entry.meaning: Invoked explicitly by the four selected parent controls through the normal libtest executable with --exact/--ignored/--nocapture/--test-threads=1; not counted as a fifth PASS or hidden product skip.
support_entry.child_lifecycle: Each parent owns its direct child and reader thread. Failure drops the receiver, kills/waits the child and joins the reader. No descendant processes are spawned; SQLite workers are threads inside that child.
support_entry.physical_resource: File::lock/try_lock on separately opened file handles in different processes; neither counters nor callback destruction alone are the lock oracle.
support_entry.budgets: New checkpoints, native callback gates, runtime entry wait and child completion use the existing candidate's five-second bound; no existing repository deadline, retry or assertion is changed.

negative_controls.name: no_worker_token
negative_controls.causal_acceptance: Both must reach their real cancellation checkpoint, observe parent try_lock succeed incorrectly, and then report gate_status=0 while the native callback is still blocked. A callback timeout/disconnection, connect completion, build failure, no tests selected or setup failure is not causal evidence.
negative_controls.not_old_source: An explicit one-line counterfactual of the final API-bearing candidate, not unmodified sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0.

negative_controls.name: unwind_releases
negative_controls.causal_acceptance: Initial error/release control must pass first; real native SQLITE_BUSY, original WorkerCrashed and subsequent SQLITE_ROW must all occur. The independent parent lock then succeeds incorrectly at busy_close_failed_and_native_statement_still_runs. Panic/setup/build/timeout before that checkpoint is not a qualified negative.
negative_controls.not_old_source: Removes only the forget-before-panic line from the final candidate. It does not suppress the original error or alter the tests.

sqlx_runtime.scope: Existing test_block_on and timeout drive the connect future; the frozen run must enable sqlx-core/_rt-tokio.

sql_safe_str.scope: Existing &'static str SqlSafeStr implementation; no ambiguous generic .into() is used.

auto_extension_binding.scope: Public tagged source exposes the real typed sqlite3_auto_extension/cancel_auto_extension callback; no function-pointer transmute. This pass did not independently extract the native libsqlite3-sys archive or run the binding.

sqlite_open_order.scope: sqlite3AutoLoadExtensions occurs inside openDatabase; the subsequent normal successful tail installs lookaside/WAL callbacks and returns. The owned child sets no SQL-log callback or other automatic extension. SQLx default establish performs native configuration and then options.connect executes initial PRAGMAs. Runtime linked SQLite identity still must be recorded.

static_validation.status: 5 sequential static git apply --check/apply phases succeeded with exact source-map reconstruction
static_validation.proof_scope: Own isolated static copies only; no Git refs, compiler, native SQLite or permission experiment.

superseded_unexecuted_drafts.reason: Static connect-driving review: keep polling through the establish oneshot until the real SQLite callback enters; use the existing flume async channel and SQLx runtime timeout, preserving the five-second native gate and physical lock assertions.
superseded_unexecuted_drafts.previous_revision_reason: Use literal &'static str directly for the actual SqlSafeStr API, avoiding ambiguous AssertSqlSafe(<literal>.into()).

next_execution_gates: Root and the sole CI owner must choose and freeze the exact dependency adoption layout and normalized package manifest. Preserve licenses, the observed package source/identity and unchanged dependency versions; do not synthesize .cargo-checksum.json or hand-edit Cargo/MODULE locks.

Run the original dependency/Bazel lock generators on that concrete adopted tree and preserve true lock change/no-change results. The current five-source patch by itself is not a project dependency adoption.

Freeze the actual driver manifest, features (bundled and sqlx-core/_rt-tokio for these four controls), source tree, real Rust/SQLite versions, original test command, exact roster and original existing driver tests. Require no early-return or selected-test skips.

Apply no_worker_token, run the first two exact controls and require the physical causal failures described above; restore exact source. Apply unwind_releases, run the fourth exact control and require its specified physical failure; restore exact source.
Run all four positive parent controls with zero retries and full raw/JUnit. Preserve the one explicit ignored support entry separately. Record child completion and actual lock checkpoints.

Run the applicable original owning state/Memory regression gates on the same adopted driver, then original fix/fmt and source/lock rechecks. Do not infer whole-workspace or platform qualification from these four controls.

Only after this dependency mechanism is qualified should a separately reviewed state/Current caller pass the real OpenGuard and demonstrate its complete resource lifetime. Native token success alone does not close B16.
